A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same NPTI method and PERSONALITYBENCH dataset. Text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable, allowing additions, removals, and relocated material to be reliably matched.

before.justification: V1 reports original NPTI experiments, including automatic and human personality evaluations, questionnaire-based alignment, cross-model comparisons, and ablations.

after.justification: V2 retains original personality-induction results and reports additional baseline comparisons, general-capability evaluations, layer ablations, timing measurements, and human dataset assessments.

M1.justification: Sections 3.2–3.3 retain the same activation-probability difference identification and weighted neuron manipulation, including Equations 1–4 and the 10% selection threshold. The new layer experiments test the existing method rather than introduce a different procedure.

E1.justification: V2 adds mathematical reasoning on GSM8K, instruction following on IFEval, and commonsense answering on CommonsenseQA. It removes the questionnaire-based personality-alignment evaluation covering 300 individuals. The main PERSONALITYBENCH generation tasks remain unchanged; IPIP-NEO still informs dataset construction.

E2.justification: ActAdd joins the automatic personality and fluency comparisons in v2 Tables 1 and 6. Removing v1 Table 3 eliminates its individual-alignment comparison suite, including PPO, DPO, and few-shot methods with GPT-4o and Llama3 results. The human-ranking comparison retains its original five methods.

E3.justification: V2 introduces base-versus-trait comparisons on general benchmarks, including zero-shot IFEval, single-layer and five-consecutive-layer controls, timing protocols, and a five-annotator dataset-quality audit. It removes the IPIP-NEO-120-guided evaluation against IPIP-NEO-300 responses using absolute score differences. The retained generation evaluation settings remain substantially unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 adds tests of which layers support personality induction, how steering affects general capabilities, and whether generated questions and descriptions are valid and unbiased. The existing weighting, gamma, and neuron-threshold ablations remain. The neurotic-and-agreeable case in v2 Table 5 was already v1 Table 19, rather than a new case study.

E5.justification: Appendix A.3 newly reports pairwise evaluator agreement for the five-judge, 200-question ranking evaluation. This adds statistical reliability reporting without establishing additional experimental runs. Existing score-variance reporting is retained, with no new seed, repeated-run, confidence-interval, or significance-test reporting.

E6.justification: Retained personality results are unchanged, including NPTI's automatic average of 9.43 and human rank of 2.27. V2 adds ActAdd results, timing, agreement, dataset-quality, layer-ablation, and general-task outcomes. For example, Table 9 reports CommonsenseQA at 69.5 under positive neuroticism versus 76.5 for the unmodified model. V1's alignment results, including NPTI's total of 3.50, disappear.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and manipulation equations in Section 3 are unchanged. Neither version provides formal theorems or proofs; the added empirical agreement calculation and experimental explanations do not introduce a theoretical development.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: PERSONALITYBENCH, identification through opposing-trait activation differences, and training-free neuron manipulation with performance comparable to supervised fine-tuning. The shortened conclusion does not materially change these claims.

C2.justification: V2 adds explanations linking conscientiousness-related gains to detailed reasoning and neuroticism-related losses to anxious responses. Appendix A.5 interprets middle-layer effects and explains the choice to manipulate all layers. It also discusses evaluation reliability and efficiency, while removing the interpretation of precise questionnaire-based alignment to individuals.

D1.justification: V2 newly documents a single A800 GPU, timing denominators, benchmark-setting references, and detailed dataset-audit recruitment, training, compensation, and annotation guidelines. Core implementation hyperparameters and the stated code-resource link remain unchanged. These additions improve documentation without establishing changes to the retained implementation.

R1.justification: V2 adds references for ActAdd, GSM8K, CommonsenseQA, IFEval, and YuLan-Mini. These support the added comparisons and evaluations; the related-work narrative and central novelty positioning remain largely unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized prose edits, shortens the conclusion, adds acknowledgments, and changes the publication header. Appendices are reorganized to place experimental results first, followed by dataset validation, prompts, and cases. Most introductory, methodological, and existing analytical prose is retained.

P2.justification: V2 adds a layer-ablation figure and tables for timing, evaluator agreement, general benchmarks, dataset quality, and annotation guidelines. Personality and fluency tables gain ActAdd columns, while the questionnaire-results table is removed. Existing displays are rearranged, an appendix case moves into the main text, and case highlights change from color to underlining.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens empirical support by adding a relevant steering baseline and checks of dataset quality, evaluator reliability, efficiency, and capability side effects. These improve credibility beyond the retained personality scores. The gain is moderated by removal of the individual-alignment evaluation and new reporting inconsistencies: Table 8 includes agreement of 0.65 despite a stated minimum of 0.67, and Appendix B's sampling description does not clearly reconcile with its reported question total.
